newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech 1996 new auto imports rise 61pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Czech 1996 new auto imports rise 61pct yr/yr.

text.p: Imports of new passenger cars to the Czech Republic in 1996 surged by 61 percent to 71,083 units, the Czech Car Importers Association (CIA) said on Friday.
It added that total imports of new light utility vehicles rose by 42 percent, year-on-year, to 15,301.

The CIA said in a preliminary report that General Motors' unit Adam Opel AG was the largest importer, with combined passenger car and utility vehicle imports of 11,507, up from 7,523 vehicles in the previous year.
Second was Germany's Volskwagen AG with 11,402 in combined imports for 1996 (7,638 in 1995), followed by Ford with a combined 10,690 (6,545 in 1995).
The report said that total sales of passenger cars only in the Czech Republic for 1996, including domestic automakers Skoda a.s., a unit of VW, was 153,907 units.
The CIA said that the rise in passenger car sales was up some 37 percent, year-on-year.
It added that the total combined sales of both passsenger and light utility vehicles was 174,815, up from 128,701 the previous year.

Skoda dominated the passenger car market in 1996 with 82,734 sold, up 22 percent, year-on-year, according to the CIA data. Total combined sales of Skoda totalled 87,390 vehicles, up from 72,078 in 1995.
